title: Manhattan-Rhapsody
identity: Denis Levaillant’s Manhattan Rhapsody is a concert work for tenor saxophone and piano, 11:40, DLM 0013, written for Jean-Michel Goury and Yves Josset. The composer’s site provides synchronized score and recording and quotes Jean-Marie Londeix recommending the work for the Londeix competition. The composer’s synchronized score/audio page is available and its first page was visually inspected. The opening bears the title Manhattan Rhapsody, tenor saxophone and piano, 2003; it begins at quarter=42, mysterioso, with a soft, slurred saxophone line over dense piano sonorities. A search-indexed composer interview in the Greensboro-hosted booklet describes seven sections, later saxophone multiphonics and slaps, a sax-piano chase, and a coda; treat those details as indexed text until the booklet can be read directly.

score_observations.observation: The composer’s synchronized opening page is labeled tenor saxophone and piano (2003), at quarter=42, mysterioso. The saxophone begins quietly with a slurred, sustained line while the piano presents dense chordal sonorities; the visible opening then shows tempo increase to quarter=52 and more active piano figuration. Only this opening sample was inspected.

review_focus: Inference from the opening score and composer-page note: review control and shape at the slow opening pulse, then ensemble coordination as the piano writing becomes more active; the indexed interview suggests later extended techniques and a sax-piano chase worth verifying in the score.
collection_flag: Original concert work with professional performance, recording, and competition recommendation. College/professional relevance is well supported.
